## Natural history notes

A small tortricid moth characterized by mottled brown to tan forewings with darker patches and wavy markings that help it blend into bark, dead leaves, and dry vegetation. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, gardens, parks, and other wooded or shrubby habitats where suitable host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed within folded or tied leaves of woody plants and shrubs, using silk shelters for protection as they develop.
